purpose: Classify support BSP placement reuse and model prepared bounds/plane storage; no production optimization or speedup claim.

metadata.profile: dev; workspace opt-level 0, Parry/Glam opt-level 3; debug info
metadata.method: Isolated per-query counters and actual published static inventories sampled at physics boundaries. One explicit warmup followed by two counted replays. No CPU/phase profiling or allocator replacement.
metadata.identity: Static owner product lineage/owner/revision/collider index. Authored shapes use Arc allocation identity pinned by Weak references, without retaining BSP child buffers. Dynamic identities preserve typed body IDs, part indices, and geometry identity; pose keys include anchor frame. No production geometry mutation via Arc::get_mut exists in these paths.
metadata.memory_limits: Additional prepared arrays retaining authored geometry. Models exclude synchronization, lookup maps, allocator bookkeeping, staging overlap, and duplicate topology. No measured process RSS or speedup claim. Spare capacity is also excluded; arrays use exact modeled lengths.

memory_models.limits: Additional arrays retain authored geometry. Float payload excludes lookup/index structures and container headers. Dense arrays include optional sphere slots per authored node, optional polygon-plane slots through the maximum polygon ID, and Vec headers. General-plane model additionally includes optional split-plane slots per node. All models exclude synchronization, topology/index mappings, allocator bookkeeping, staging overlap, and other query families. First-use peak is reconstructed at replay physics boundaries, not measured RSS.

interpretation: Static products account for 98.136% of support bounds transforms and 97.054% of polygon-plane transforms. Resident product identity and exact static transforms remain unchanged during repeated queries.

All 292 resident static BSP parts model 558496 bytes of dense support bounds/polygon-plane arrays. The 38 support-queried parts model 77464 bytes. These are payload scenarios, not measured heap/RSS or complete implementation budgets.
Unqueried means unqueried by support; camera, sweeps, recovery, and other collision families may use additional parts.
Four entity BSP query records each have one observed frame pose and no observed pose changes. This fixture does not qualify performance for moving or animated BSP targets.

Dynamic target preparation constructs 110231 BSP shapes from 32 distinct geometry/frame/pose combinations. Do not attach eager prepared arrays to the generic placed-shape constructor without a separate lifetime/reuse design.

The next bounded experiment is static resident preparation of node bounds and polygon planes, owned by the world scene product lifetime. Keep authored content lossless and leave dynamic target preparation unchanged. Compare eager static preparation with first-use preparation only if the extra lifecycle machinery earns its cost.
Measure actual memory, residency publication work, and clean paired runtime performance before retention. Do not infer a CPU speedup from transform counts.

previous_probe_comparison.explanation: Keep both datasets. The earlier intrusive census shifted simulated poses slightly; this lighter per-query census matches the clean reference exactly. Polygon-plane and polygon-vertex totals agree, while visited bounds differ by 18.
